cleanIntro: The P-10 F is the full-size P-10 — the only one in the family CZ zeroes at 25 m rather than 15, and one of the two sizes cleared for a standard-size suppressor. The strip itself is the P-10 line's: trigger pulled and held rearward, slide back 5 mm, disassembly plate down, slide forward off the frame. Everything below is read off the English section of CZ's P-10 manual, PDF pages 2 to 14.

steps.title: Confirm the F size and the build in front of you
steps.action: Read the slide legend and the muzzle. CZ's P-10 book covers the standard pistol plus the Ported, Optics Ready, Suppressor Ready and Optics & Suppressor Ready builds; establish which one your F is before you strip it, because the parts on the bench will not be the same set on all of them.
steps.prose: The F is the duty-length P-10 and the longest slide and barrel in the family, which is why it and the SC are the two sizes CZ clears for a full-size can. A Ported F has a compensator port cut through slide and barrel near the muzzle and a bore that is no longer a plain tube. An Optics Ready F has a milled slide interface with a cover plate that is itself a listed part, so the number of screws you find on top of the slide is a version question and not a fault.
steps.caution: CZ marks the slide, barrel, magazine catch and its plug, the trigger bar disconnector, the frame, the recoil spring, the sight screws, the front sight, the magazine, the cover with screws and the thread guard as version-dependent. Determine which of those are present on your own P-10 F rather than working from the full list.
steps.quote: The parts marked * differ according to versions, or as case may be in some versions are entirely missing.
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — List of Parts, closing note, p.13

steps.title: The F takes a standard-size can — the C does not
steps.action: If a suppressor is fitted, take it off before stripping and check its size class against the pistol. CZ specifies a compact size suppressor for the P-10 C; the SC and F sizes are the ones cleared to run a standard size can as well.
steps.prose: The full-size slide and its heavier reciprocating mass are what make the F tolerant of a standard can, so this is one of the few places where owning the F genuinely changes what you may hang on the muzzle. Suppressed shooting still costs the pistol something: if this F is fired only with a can and a reflex sight, CZ wants the return spring assembly replaced preventatively every 2,000 rounds, and the suppressor's tightness on the thread checked after no more than two full magazines. When the can is off, the muzzle thread gets its cap back on before the gun goes away.
steps.quote: using a compact size sound suppressor for the CZ P-10 C pistol; the SC and F versions can also be used with a standard size sound suppressor
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Pistol Description — Optics & Suppressor Ready recommendations, p.6
steps.warn: A reflex sight fitted to the OR interface on the slide is limited to 35 g maximum weight, and CZ wants the mounting plate screws torqued to 1.3 Nm with thread glue.

steps.title: Magazine out, and do not slap it home to test it
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction, depress the ambidextrous magazine catch and let the magazine fall out of the frame. Put it down; the pistol must not be disassembled with a magazine in it.
steps.prose: The full-size P-10 magazine is a long column and a loaded one drops fast and heavy — keep a hand under the well. CZ's rule that the well must be empty is mechanical rather than ceremonial: the disassembly plate sits in the frame above the magazine and cannot travel down against a magazine body. There is a second warning worth heeding on an F, whose well accepts more than one magazine length: slapping a magazine that was not designed for that frame size shortens the life of the cartridge ejector.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine. The pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted!
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Rack, inspect the chamber, then the deliberate dry press
steps.action: Draw the slide fully to the rear and confirm by eye and by finger that the last cartridge has been extracted and ejected. Let the slide run forward, then pull the trigger as an aimed safety shot into a safe area.
steps.prose: On the full-size slide the ejection port is long enough that a live round usually leaves cleanly, which is exactly why people stop watching — follow the round out and account for it. CZ's unloading sequence ends in a dry press, and on the P-10 that press does double duty: it also releases the striker and puts the trigger where the strip needs it. A P-10 gives you no hammer to read, so the chamber inspection has to be done with your eyes, not by inference.
steps.quote: Draw back the slide and verify the last cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Unloading the Pistol, p.8
steps.warn: MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER — CZ prints this as its own numbered step in the strip, between removing the magazine and pulling the trigger.

steps.title: The F is the 25 m gun — know that before you touch the sights
steps.action: Note the factory zero distance for this pistol before cleaning near the sights: CZ zeroed the P-10 F at 25 m, where the rest of the P-10 line leaves the factory zeroed at 15 m. Windage is corrected by drifting the rear sight in its dovetail and locking it with its screw; elevation by changing the front sight for a taller or shorter blade.
steps.prose: This is the single P-10 specification that is different for the F and it is easy to lose during maintenance rather than at the range. Both sights are held by small screws, and a brush dragged across a rear sight in a dovetail can shift a windage setting by more than you will notice on the bench. Some P-10 versions use sights that are not screw-secured at all, so check yours before assuming there is a screw holding anything. Wipe the sights clean; do not scrub them, and do not solvent-soak a tritium or fibre insert.
steps.quote: The pistol sights were sighted in at the manufacturing plant at a distance of 15 m (CZ P-10 F at 25 m) so that the mean point of impact approximately conforms to the point of aim.
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Sight Adjustment, p.8

steps.title: Trigger pulled, and confirmed sitting back
steps.action: Pull the trigger and check that it stays in the rear position. With the striker already released it will rest there; if it snaps forward, the slide has re-cocked the striker and you need another dry press before continuing.
steps.prose: Everything that follows depends on this. With the trigger back the trigger bar is dropped clear of the slide's path; with it forward, the disassembly plate feels seized and people start pushing harder on the wrong part. This is a check, not a force — a trigger visibly resting against the rear of its guard is the whole confirmation. On the F the trigger guard is roomy enough that you can see the gap behind the trigger directly.
steps.quote: 3. Pull the trigger and make sure that it remains in the rear position.
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 3, p.9

steps.title: Move the slide back 5 mm — a nudge, not a rack
steps.action: Wrap your palm round the frame and use the fingers of the same hand to grip the rear of the slide from above. Move the slide rearward by no more than 5 mm and hold it exactly there.
steps.prose: Five millimetres is about the width of one rear serration group on the F's slide, and the tolerance is real: too far and the plate's clearance cut has passed its window, too little and the slide still traps the plate. The full-size slide gives you a good grip and a long spring, so it is easy to overshoot — set the distance first, then hold it while the other hand works. If the plate refuses to move, back off and reset the 5 mm rather than pressing harder.
steps.quote: 4. Grasp the frame with your palm, use the fingers of the same hand to grasp the rear part of the slide from the top. Use your fingers to move the slide back by no more than 5 mm (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 4, p.9

steps.title: Disassembly plate straight down to its stop
steps.action: Holding that 5 mm of slide travel, push the disassembly plate downwards with the fingers of your free hand until it reaches its stop. Both ends of the plate travel together.
steps.prose: The plate is the flat tab standing proud of the frame on both sides just above the trigger; it slides, it does not rotate, and it is not the slide stop sitting behind it. Its travel is short and it ends against a hard stop you will feel — that stop is the signal to move on, and pushing beyond it only bends the plate spring. A plate that will not start moving is telling you about the trigger or the 5 mm, not about itself.
steps.quote: 5. Use the fingers of your other hand to push the disassembly plate downwards until it stops. (Fig. 8).
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 5, p.9

steps.title: Let the slide go forward off the frame
steps.action: Release your grip on the slide and run it forward off the front of the frame, keeping the muzzle in a safe direction and both hands on the slide as it separates.
steps.prose: With the plate down there is nothing retaining the slide, and the recoil spring pushes it forward for you — guide it, do not haul it. Do not lift the rear of the slide first; the F's rails are long and levering one end scores them. The plate springs back up on its own once the slide has left, so there is no lever to return and no part to reset.
steps.quote: 6. Release the pressure on the slide and remove it from the frame (Fig. 9)
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, p.9

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out, then the barrel
steps.action: Invert the slide. Lift the captive recoil spring assembly out at the muzzle end first and let its tension off gradually, then lift the barrel free of the slide.
steps.prose: That order is fixed by the geometry: the recoil spring assembly bears on the barrel lug, so the barrel is trapped until the spring is out. The F's assembly is the longest in the family and carries real stored energy even captive — hold it at both ends coming out rather than letting it pivot. When it is done you have the four pieces CZ's procedure yields: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, with the magazine already aside.
steps.quote: 7. Remove the recoil spring from the slide and finally the barrel.
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 7, p.9

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly on the bench with the magazine set aside. That is the entire field strip CZ publishes for the P-10 F — the striker assembly, trigger bar, extractor and back straps all stay in the gun.
steps.prose: Those four pieces open up everything the cleaning section asks for: the bore and chamber approached from the breech, the breech face and extractor, the inside of the slide and the frame rails, and the full outside of the barrel. CZ closes the strip by saying routine maintenance needs nothing more, and that firing pin cleaning belongs to a gunsmith rather than to the owner. The one further job the book does hand you is stripping the magazine after a heavy session.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges has been fired, it is advisable to also disassemble magazine and to entrust the pistol to a competent gunsmith for the firing pin cleaning.
steps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, closing note, p.9

deepSteps.title: Identify which magazine base design the F carries
deepSteps.action: Look at the base of the magazine. Either it has a hole with the base lock showing through it, or the rear of the magazine carries a sliding base lock. On the holed type, push the lock in through the hole and slide the base slightly forward.
deepSteps.prose: CZ builds both patterns and the handling differs, so identify before you push — a punch used on a sliding-lock magazine only marks the polymer. On the sliding type you move the lock into its disassembly position first and then walk the base forward. The full-size F magazine is a long column and holds proportionally more fouling under the follower than a compact one, which is why the book puts this job after a heavy session rather than after every range trip.
deepSteps.quote: There is a difference depending on the magazine design. If there is a hole in the magazine base, push the base lock through the hole and slide the base slightly forward.
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Thumb on the base, spring released under control
deepSteps.action: Cover the base with your thumb to hold the spring, then use the other hand to slide the base completely off its guiding rails. Let your thumb up slowly so the spring rises rather than launches.
deepSteps.prose: The F's magazine spring is long and fully compressed by the base; releasing it without a thumb on top sends base, spring and follower in three directions at once. Do this over a bench with the magazine mouth pointed away from your face. Watch the follower's orientation as it clears — it is handed, and a follower reinstalled upside down presents the first round nose-high and will stop the pistol on the first shot.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the base with your thumb to hold the spring and use the other hand to slide the base completely out of its guiding rails. Be careful during the disassembly as the spring could fly out, or even cause an injury.
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Dry-clean the magazine, then stop
deepSteps.action: Wipe the inside of the magazine body, the follower and the spring with a dry cloth or a brass bristle brush and leave them dry. Reassemble the magazine and go no deeper into the pistol.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside a magazine body holds grit against the cases and gums the follower, and on an F that shows up as a sluggish last round rather than a failure you can see. While the magazine is apart, sight along the feed lips against a known-good magazine; a lip that has spread is a magazine to retire rather than to bend. Once it is back together, that is the boundary of owner maintenance in this book.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended. Should your pistol require adjustment or repair be sure the task is entrusted to a competent gunsmith!
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-10 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — CAUTION following Magazine Disassembly, p.10
deepSteps.warn: CZ lists the firing pin assembly's seven sub-parts but does not give the owner a procedure for it — that job is named as a gunsmith's throughout the book.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Push a clean patch on a rod through the bore and chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean — enough on its own if the F has fired only a few rounds
For a heavily fouled bore, brush gun cleaning solution in, let it work about 10 minutes, then scrub the bore out thoroughly
Insert rod and brush from the CHAMBER end and drive the brush right out of the muzzle before reversing; changing direction inside the barrel is how a brush jams
On a Ported F, clean the compensator port through both slide and barrel as well as the rifling — it carbons up faster than the bore does
Dry the bore and chamber with a clean patch and confirm all powder residue and fouling are gone before oiling

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & FRAME
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, brass bristle brush or a wooden scraper on the breech face, the extractor claw and its recess, the slide's inner rails and the frame rails
Preserving or paraffin oil may be used here — never the barrel bore cleaning agent, which lingers in the joints and corrodes them later
Wipe down the outside of the barrel including the locking lug and the barrel hood
Check no cloth particles or brush bristles have lodged in the pistol before it goes back together
If the roll pins of the front or rear insert have been out at any point, fit new roll pins rather than the old ones

cleaning.name: OIL & WIPE DOWN
tasks: With bore, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or spray it on, then remove all excess
At very low temperatures take the oil off every accessible part or use a lubricant made for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in a demanding climate only, and comes off every part before the pistol is used again
Wipe the bore dry before shooting

reassembly: Barrel into the inverted slide first, then the recoil spring assembly onto the barrel lug — the assembly will not seat if the barrel is not fully home.
Put the trigger to the rear (pulled) position BEFORE the slide goes on; CZ's note is that this prevents the frame colliding with the protrusion on the trigger bar.
Run the slide onto the frame from the front, take it fully back and let it go forward under its own spring; the disassembly plate returns up by itself.
Rack once to reset trigger and striker, then confirm the trigger returns forward and resets.
Dry-patch the bore before the F is carried or fired, and refit the muzzle cap if the thread is bare.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty: the slide should travel its full length with no downward creep from the disassembly plate; the trigger safety blade should stand proud and block the trigger until it is pressed; a dry press should be followed by an audible, felt reset as the slide is eased forward; the striker should stay blocked with the trigger untouched; and an empty magazine should lock the slide back on the slide stop, which should release cleanly from either side. Check the rear sight has not shifted in its dovetail if a brush went near it — the F's 25 m zero is easy to lose on the bench.
